current_activity: returning to England after the Normandy campaign
notes: CMH ETO-OB command post list: division CP at Newbury (Greenham Lodge) from 15 July 1944; the assignment table shows Ninth Army from the same date.

current_activity: passing to XVIII Airborne Corps and First Allied Airborne Army
notes: CMH ETO-OB assignment table dated 12 August 1944. Location is the last CP listed (Greenham Lodge, since 15 July).

current_activity: parachute and glider landing between Son and Veghel (Market Garden)
notes: Event date: CMH ETO-OB dates the Market Garden landing 17 September 1944; CMH lists the division CP at Zon (Son) on that date (see the separate hq_move row). Event definition: the airborne landing, spread between Son, Sint-Oedenrode and Veghel; the point is the centre of that area (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, Sint-Oedenrode centroid), not the command post this row used before. Relationship: British XXX Corps took control on 18 September per the CMH table; the division was under British I Airborne Corps (operational control) with XVIII Airborne Corps in England.

current_activity: division command post at Zon after the landing
notes: Event date: CMH ETO-OB CP list: Zon (Son) on 17 September 1944. Event definition: the division command post, not the landing (separate row C0220). Location: town centroid of Zon; the command post site is not given. Relationship: as on C0220.

current_activity: division command post at Sint-Oedenrode
notes: CMH ETO-OB CP list: St-Oedenrode from 20 September 1944. CMH shows the division under British XXX Corps (from 18 September) and I Airborne Corps (21 September).

current_activity: CMH table lists the division under British I Airborne Corps from 21 September
notes: Event date: 21 September 1944 (the CMH ETO-OB order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division lists "Br I ABN" in its corps column from 21 September, "Br VIII" from 23 September). Event definition: a table observation, not an operational event; added on 26 October 2026 as the evidence of CR0376 because no other claim lies between 20 September (C0221) and the next table row. Relationship: British I Airborne Corps, unspecified_subordination (CR0376); First Allied Airborne Army assigned and British Second Army attached (table; CR0102, CR0106). XVIII Airborne Corps stays the corps of record in the table only until 17 September (CR0103, CR0104). Location: the division command post was at St-Oedenrode from 20 September (C0221; the CMH command-post list has no entry for 21 or 22 September, the next is Veghel on 24 September); the point is the town centroid, and no source places the command post elsewhere on 21 September. Coordinates as C0221 (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, St-Oedenrode). Event support: low (a table date). Location support: low (an inference from the previous command post).

current_activity: CMH table lists the division under British VIII Corps from 23 September
notes: Event date: 23 September 1944 (the CMH ETO-OB order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division (R336) lists "Br VIII" in its corps column from 23 September; "Br I ABN" from 21 September, "Br XII" from 28 September). Event definition: a table observation, not an operational event; added on 26 October 2026 (open item 7, the 101st's October-November rows) as the evidence of CR0377 because no claim lies on that date. Relationship: British VIII Corps, unspecified_subordination (CR0377); First Allied Airborne Army assigned and British Second Army attached (table; CR0102, CR0106). Location: the division command post was at St-Oedenrode from 20 September (C0221) and the CMH list has no later entry before Veghel on 24 September; the point is the town centroid. Coordinates as C0221 (OpenStreetMap Nominatim). Event support: low (a table date). Location support: low (an inference from the previous command post, one day before the next).

current_activity: division command post at Veghel
notes: CMH ETO-OB CP list: Vechel (Veghel) from 24 September 1944. Added on 26 October 2026 (open item 7). The CMH spells the town Vechel. Location: town (municipality) centroid; the command post site is not given. Relationship: as on C0568 (British VIII Corps from 23 September, table).

current_activity: CMH table lists the division under British XII Corps from 28 September
notes: Event date: 28 September 1944 (the CMH ETO-OB order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division (R336) lists "Br XII" in its corps column from 28 September; "Cdn II" from 9 November). current_activity: division command post at Slijk-Ewijk (the Island)
notes: CMH ETO-OB CP list: Slik Ewjik from 5 October 1944, listed with the region Nord Brabant. Added on 26 October 2026 (open item 7). Location: the only place of that name found is Slijk-Ewijk, Gelderland (place PL0385, village centroid), on the Nijmegen-Arnhem Island where the division served in October; the CMH region is read as an error and the confidence is 0.5 for that reason. The CMH list has no entry between 5 October and 1 December (C0573). Relationship: as on C0570 (British XII Corps, table).

current_activity: CMH table lists the division under II Canadian Corps and First Canadian Army from 9 November
notes: Event date: 9 November 1944 (the CMH ETO-OB order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division (R336) lists "Cdn II" in its corps column and "Cdn First" in the Army Attached column from 9 November, until the row of 17 December). Event definition: a table observation, not an operational event; added on 26 October 2026 (open item 7, the 101st's October-November rows) as the evidence of CR0379 and CR0380 because no claim lies on that date. Relationship: II Canadian Corps unspecified_subordination (CR0379) and First Canadian Army attached (CR0380), replacing British XII Corps and British Second Army (CR0378, CR0106); First Allied Airborne Army assigned (table). Location: the last CMH command post before the date is Slijk-Ewijk (5 October, C0571); the point is the village centroid. The CMH list puts the command post at Mourmelon on 1 December (C0573), so the division had left the Netherlands before the Canadian entries end; see C0573. Event support: low (a table date). Location support: low (an inference from the previous command post, five weeks earlier).

current_activity: division command post at Mourmelon (the division is back in France)
notes: CMH ETO-OB CP list: Mourmelon, Marne from 1 December 1944. Added on 26 October 2026 (open item 7). Location: the CMH gives the town; the point is the centroid of Mourmelon-le-Grand (place PL0238, as C0563). Relationship: the CMH table still lists II Canadian Corps and First Canadian Army for the division on this date (CR0379, CR0380; the table's next row is 17 December), although the command post was at Mourmelon, in France; the table's Canadian entries after the move are probably not updated (an inference: no source says when the division left the Canadian corps), and they are kept as the table has them.

current_activity: CMH table lists the division under VIII Corps from 17 December while it is still at Camp Mourmelon
notes: Event date: 17 December 1944 (the CMH ETO order-of-battle table for the 101st Airborne Division lists VIII Corps in its corps column from 17 December). Event definition: a table observation, not an operational transfer. The table date is an assignment date; the Green Book has the division in SHAEF reserve under the XVIII Airborne Corps, the alert reaching the corps chief of staff in the early evening of 17 December (Ardennes p304), the division leaving Camp Mourmelon that night, and Hodges turning it over to Middleton's VIII Corps on 18 December (p306). The operational passage to VIII Corps is on the 19 December row (C0553) and the passage of VIII Corps to Third Army on the 20 December row (C0554). An earlier version of this row was an alternate in conflict group G016 against C0554; the two rows record different things on different dates (a table classification and an operational event), so the group is dissolved and the rows are a sequence. Relationship: XVIII Airborne Corps is the operational parent on 17 December; VIII Corps unspecified_subordination from 17 December (CMH table, start between 17 and 18 December); First Allied Airborne Army assigned (table). The CMH table also lists Third Army and 12th Army Group as attached from 17 December; that is not encoded here, because the Green Book dates the corps' passage to Third Army on 20 December and a table classification three days earlier is not control by Third Army. The Third Army entry begins on C0554. Location: Camp Mourmelon (Mourmelon-le-Grand): the atlas lists the division there on 1 December and the Green Book has it moving out on the night of 18 December; no source places it elsewhere on 17 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Mourmelon-le-Grand. Event support: low (a table date, contradicted as an operational date by narrative pages). Location support: low (an inference from the departure; the atlas entry is 16 days earlier).

current_activity: arrives at Bastogne by truck from Camp Mourmelon; all four regiments in hand by 0900
notes: Event date: 19 December 1944 (Ardennes p308: the move from Camp Mourmelon to Bastogne, 107 miles, with the 501st detrucking at midnight; "By 0900 on 19 December McAuliffe had all four regiments in hand"). Event definition: the 101st Airborne Division, held in SHAEF reserve at Mourmelon, is committed to the VIII Corps at Bastogne; this is the division's arrival at the town, not the encirclement (21 December). Relationship: VIII Corps operational_control from 18 December (Ardennes p306: Hodges turned the division over to Middleton; the CMH table lists VIII Corps from 17 December, C0563); the corps is under First Army until it passes to Third Army on 20 December (C0546, C0554); First Allied Airborne Army assigned. The CMH table lists Third Army attached from 17 December; that is a table classification and is not encoded before the Green Book's 20 December passage. Location: Bastogne town centroid; the atlas lists the division at Bastogne on 19 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bastogne. Event support: high (Green Book and atlas agree). Location support: high for the date and place (a division command post in the town). Command support: the VIII Corps start is a narrative date without an hour (p306); the table date is 17 December.

current_activity: VIII Corps and the 101st at Bastogne pass from First Army to Third Army during the day
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p399: "The VIII Corps passed to General Patton's Third Army during the 20th", with some confusion among the units attached to the corps about their exact status; p456: planning at Bastogne that day). The hour is not documented. Event definition: the corps, and with it the 101st Airborne at Bastogne, passes from Hodges' First Army to Patton's Third Army at an undocumented hour of 20 December. The 101st's immediate parent is VIII Corps throughout (operational_control from 18 December, C0553); Third Army's authority over the division is inherited through the corps from the passage, not asserted separately for any earlier day. The question 'who controlled the division at noon on 20 December' is therefore unknown at army level (First Army before the passage, Third Army after it) and scripts/who_controls.py reports it as such. An earlier version of this row was the preferred half of conflict group G016; with the CMH table row reclassified as a table observation (C0563) the group is dissolved. Relationship: VIII Corps operational_control from 18 December; First Allied Airborne Army assigned (table); Third Army attached from 20 December (Green Book), against 17 December in the CMH table, a documented disagreement in which the narrative date is used; 12th Army Group attached through Third Army. Location: Bastogne, the division command post (atlas 19 December; Ardennes p456 for 20 December planning at Bastogne). Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bastogne. Event support: moderate (the day is documented; the hour is not, and the table date disagrees). Location support: high (command post at Bastogne for the day).

current_activity: Bastogne is surrounded; the division holds a perimeter around the town
notes: Event date: 21 December 1944 (Ardennes p458: "by daylight on the 21st the German infantry following the armored troops were ensconced on both the main roads running from Bastogne south", while in the north the circle had been clamped shut during the preceding hours). Event definition: the road net around Bastogne is cut and the 101st Airborne (with attached armor and the VIII Corps remnants) is encircled; the row dates the first full day of the encirclement, not the German first contact on the 20th. Relationship: VIII Corps operational_control (C0553); Third Army attached from 20 December and exercised through the corps (C0554). Location: The atlas lists the division command post at Bastogne on 19 December and nothing else for the siege; no source places the command post anywhere but the town until the relief. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bastogne. Event support: high (Green Book narrative). Location support: moderate (the town is certain; the atlas entry for the post is two days earlier).

current_activity: the division enters Noville in the fighting for the north-eastern part of the Bulge
notes: Event date: 15 January 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 2 p. 42: on 15 January the 101st Airborne Division entered Noville). Event definition: the division retakes Noville north-east of Bastogne; the CMH table keeps it under VIII Corps until 18 January. Relationship: VIII Corps operational_control (CR0110, standing relation); Third Army attached (CR0112, standing relation); First Allied Airborne Army assigned (from 12 Aug 44, CMH table); 12th Army Group attached (CR0111, standing relation). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). Location: Noville, near Bastogne. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Noville, Luxembourg). Event support: moderate (single Green Book sentence). Location support: moderate (named village).

current_activity: command post at Miesbach as the paratroopers approach Berchtesgaden
notes: Event date: 4 May 1945 (CMH ETO-OB command-post list of the 101st Airborne Division: Miesbach on 4 May 45; Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 441-442: the XV Corps drove for Salzburg and Berchtesgaden; a photograph shows paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division approaching Berchtesgaden; ch. 19 p. 474: after dark on 6 May SS troops seized three men of the division and released them the next morning). Event definition: the division command post is at Miesbach on the date; the Green Book does not give the day of the division's entry into Berchtesgaden in the passages read. Relationship: XXI Corps unspecified_subordination (from 4 May 45, CMH table); Seventh Army attached (from 17 Apr 45, CMH table); First Allied Airborne Army assigned (from 12 Aug 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group attached (from 17 Apr 45, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier operational_control relation to VIII Corps (CR0110) is closed at 18 January 1945 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Miesbach (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R336 p. 387: listed 4 May 1945); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Miesbach. Event support: weak (the Green Book pages give a photograph caption and a later incident, not the division's own movement; the CMH list gives the place). Location support: moderate (command post listed on the date).
